newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AGASSI DECIDES TO MISS 1997 AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI DECIDES TO MISS 1997 AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: U.S. tennis ace Andre Agassi has decided he needs a break from tennis and will not compete in next January's Australian Open grand slam event, which he won in 1995, the tournament director said on Friday.
Agassi will begin his 1997 tennis campaign after the Australian Open, said director Paul McNamee.

"It's disappointing that Andre will not be playing, but he clearly feels he needs some time off," said McNamee in a statement. "I'm encouraged that Andre considers this to be one-off and intends to be back in 1998."

Agassi has played in only two Australian Opens. After winning the tournament in his first appearance in 1995, the 26-year-old from Las Vegas was beaten in the semifinals by fellow American Michael Chang this year.

The Australian Open, won by Germany's Boris Becker in 1996, is held between January 13 and 26. Both Becker and Monica Seles, winner of this year's women's singles title, have said they will defend their titles.
